calculation.properties: Pure standard library; exact Fraction arithmetic; deterministic JSON stdout only; no timestamps, files, network, randomness, third-party libraries, or author code. Output density pieces and masses are derived by transport, not hardcoded.
checks: 576 positive finite-target cases with two symmetric proposal families, four drifts and deterministic/two-point independent noise: wrapped translation plus acceptance rescaling preserves the complete piecewise-constant joint density exactly.

Two-state symmetric flip with target (1/3,2/3): correct rescaling gives joint densities 1/6 and 1/3 uniformly over (-1,1). Omitting rescaling breaks the product joint density after one step and gives state-0 probability 1/6 instead of 1/3 after a second fixed-threshold step.
Asymmetric proposal negative control [[1/2,1/2],[1,0]] gives state-0 probability 1/2 under the density-ratio-only rule, demonstrating that the symmetric-proposal boundary is substantive.

Half-period drift is an involution on v, but the full shift-then-accept chain has unequal exact set fluxes 1/24 and 0. Full independent v refresh followed by acceptance/rescaling has another pair of unequal augmented-state fluxes, 1/192 and 1/384, even though the projected x process uses ordinary Metropolis transitions.

The three-state complete graph without self loops has an irreducible aperiodic reversible baseline but its equation-defined pair lift has two closed deterministic orientation classes. Local balance, off-diagonal domination and pair invariance hold. Each class in this example still has the correct projected marginal, so this is specifically an expanded-irreducibility counterexample.
Point-mass conditionals are handled without division by zero; the two-state alternating example retains the required previous conditional state after the swap.

Conditional row (3/5,3/10,1/10) with current index 0: Eq.(16) gives row (29/63,3/7,1/9). The printed p.9 first-branch acceptance for index 1 is 10/7; clipping produces 3/10 instead of the required 3/7 transition. The diagonal remains 29/63, illustrating suppression without complete elimination.

54 positive symmetric-conductance baseline families: exact row normalization, detailed balance, positive-support lifting, conditional invariance, off-diagonal domination and expanded irreducibility checked. Exact Poisson-equation asymptotic-variance calculations for all three coordinate indicators give 162 valid comparisons, each strictly improved. These finite illustrations do not prove the general theorem or wall-clock benefits.
calculation.limitations: Finite positive targets and continuous auxiliary-density transport only; no simulated trajectories or empirical autocorrelation estimates. No verification of author scripts, numerical experiments, arbitrary general MH extensions, continuous-state irreducibility, or the complete general asymptotic-variance proof. The Poisson equation is applied only after exact finite irreducibility checks.

findings.owner: handoff / future candidate wording; no maintained record defect existed at assignment
findings.locator: Neal2020 Section 2 p.2 Eq.(1); handoff candidate limitations about zero shift, half-period shift and uniform regeneration
findings.finding: The translation substep is reversible for deterministic drift congruent to 0 or 1 modulo 2, but that fact does not establish reversibility of the composed augmented chain. Uniform regeneration recovers ordinary Metropolis for the x projection, but also does not establish augmented-chain detailed balance. The handoff's wording is ambiguous if interpreted as a statement about the entire method.
findings.evidence: The exact calculator has unequal stationary set fluxes for both half-period-shift-then-accept and refresh-then-accept compositions. Composition of invariant reversible kernels need not be reversible.
findings.recommendation: State degeneracy only for the threshold update; distinguish the full (x,v) chain and the x projection. Do not claim every invariant tuning is nonreversible or every reversible threshold substep makes the complete chain reversible.

findings.locator: Neal2020 Section 2 p.2 acceptance rule and Eq.(2); random-walk proposal p.3; augmented reversible proposal Section 4 p.5
findings.finding: The simple density-ratio acceptance/rescaling construction needs a symmetric proposal independent of the persistent v, or an appropriately reversible volume-preserving augmented proposal. Mere symmetry in x at each fixed v is insufficient if the proposal law changes between the forward and rescaled reverse v values.
findings.evidence: For independent symmetric q, accepted transport has forward density pi(y)q(x,y)/2 after the v Jacobian and matches the reverse flow when q(x,y)=q(y,x). The asymmetric-q negative control fails invariance. No general q-ratio extension was established in this audit.
findings.recommendation: Keep the existing symmetric-proposal or valid augmented-proposal boundary explicit; do not generalize the simple rule to arbitrary MALA/asymmetric proposals.

findings.finding: Local conditional reversibility and off-diagonal domination do not imply expanded-state irreducibility. The later paper explicitly adds that condition before retaining the variance order.
findings.recommendation: Require expanded irreducibility separately for the stated single-coordinate asymptotic-variance comparison. Distinguish invariance from ergodicity and asymptotic per-transition variance from finite-run error or wall-clock cost.

mathematical_rationale.persistent_uniform: For a symmetric proposal independent of v, an accepted move x->y maps v to v*pi(x)/pi(y). Its inverse Jacobian is pi(y)/pi(x), so joint input density pi(x)/2 times q(x,y) transforms to pi(y)/2 times q(x,y), matching reverse flow. Rejections retain the full state. Independent wrapped translations preserve uniform v conditionally on x, so composition preserves pi(x)Uniform(-1,1). Invariance does not imply full-chain reversibility or convergence.
mathematical_rationale.backtracking_lift: The baseline detailed balance gives mu(a,b)=pi(b)T(b,a). Conditional invariance gives sum_a T(b,a)U_b(a,c)=T(b,c). Consequently the shift/update chain preserves mu(b,c)=pi(b)T(b,c). Off-diagonal domination reduces the diagonal return probability, but says nothing sufficient about connectedness of the expanded state graph.
